audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 was marked Sylas in both layers while the packet chart says Ryze, and the mirror audit already moved that row to Ryze.
audit.why: The row was written on the false premise that Hijack removes Ryze's ultimate. Sylas 55.05% over 545 games — the lane is won before 6, not at it.
audit.corrected: Row 4 to Ryze in both layers, rating 7/10 to 4/10 (inverse of the mirror's 6/10).

audit.whatIsWrong: The page treats level 6 as the Sylas spike: 'You steal Realm Warp and Ryze is suddenly a stationary poke mage with no disengage and no global.'
audit.why: Sylas's R copies an enemy ultimate; it does not remove it. Ryze keeps Realm Warp. And Realm Warp itself is a 180/160/140s repositioning portal with no damage and no CC, so the copy adds nothing to a duel.
audit.corrected: Your real spikes are level 2-3 (E online) and Riftmaker. Level 6 is a Ryze spike here because your ultimate is worth the least it can possibly be worth.
sources: champ-data/_kits/sylas.json (R text: 'steals the enemy's ultimate ability and can cast it freely')

audit.whatIsWrong: Rune Prison is called a 'point-blank root' everywhere. It is 615 range, and it only roots if the target already has Flux on them — otherwise it slows.
audit.why: Riot text: 'Ryze traps a target in a cage of runes, damaging them and slowing their movement. If the target has Flux on it, they are instead rooted.' Spell Flux is 615 range on 3.5/3.25/3/2.75/2.5.
audit.corrected: The gate is Spell Flux, not Rune Prison. No Flux on you, no root — Rune Prison is a slow you can walk through. Bait the Flux and step in during its 2.5-3.5s downtime.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ryze.json (W and E text, ranges, cooldowns)

audit.whatIsWrong: tradeBad and dontsFull describe Sylas's E as giving a 'stun'.
audit.why: Riot's text for Abscond/Abduct is a dash with a recast chain-pull; derived flags list dash and projectile, no hardCC. The mirror auditor flagged the same and removed the phrasing rather than assert the negative.
audit.corrected: Replaced with the real loss condition — no shield, no gap-close, standing inside Overload's 1000 range.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown numbers on the abilities the lane is played around.
audit.why: Overload 5s and reset by every other spell at 1000 range; Spell Flux 3.5 down to 2.5; Rune Prison 11/10.5/10/9.5/9; Realm Warp 180/160/140.
audit.corrected: Added to breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d and dontsFull[1].d — Overload is not punishable, Spell Flux barely is, Rune Prison is the only cooldown worth counting.

audit.whatIsWrong: dontsFull bodies do not match their titles — dontsFull[2] is titled 'Sit on a stolen ult' and its body describes engaging with no E charges.
audit.corrected: Rewrote both to match their titles with the real Realm Warp and Overload numbers.

edits.before: Hijack online — you now own a copy of Ryze's ultimate. The all-in math and every 2v2 swing your way.
edits.after: Hijack copies Realm Warp — a 180s portal, not a fight-winner. Level 6 gives Ryze more than it gives you.

edits.before: Hijacking Realm Warp is the defining moment: Ryze loses his only escape and you hold his global, swinging every all-in and skirmish your way.
edits.after: Hijack copies, it does not steal: Ryze keeps Realm Warp and you gain a 180s portal that wins no duel, so his 6 is worth more than yours here.

edits.before: Ryze's Realm Warp is a liability — you hijack it and leave him with no escape and no disengage while you have his own global on your bar.
edits.after: Realm Warp is the worst ult on the map to hijack — a 180s repositioning portal with no damage and no CC, so treat level 6 as Ryze's spike, not yours.

edits.before: At level 6 this lane flips hard in tempo. You steal Realm Warp and Ryze is suddenly a stationary poke mage with no disengage and no global — every all-in threat is now yours. Use the Hijacked Realm Warp tactically: hold it to deny his escape when you dive, or burn it to set up a cross-map play while he is stuck top. Keep baiting Rune Prison, let it whiff or land on a position you planned for, then E2-hook-W for the kill. Doran's Shield or a early Verdant Barrier nullifies his Q spam and lets you out-sustain the poke war. Force the all-in before his Tear stack finishes.
edits.after: At level 6 nothing flips. Hijack copies Realm Warp, it does not take it — Ryze keeps his ultimate and you gain a 180-second portal with no damage and no CC, which wins you no duel. Use it as a map tool: reposition your team or cut off his walk home, not as a combat opener. The lane still turns on Spell Flux. Rune Prison is a 615-range slow until Flux is on you, and only then a root, so bait the Flux out and step in during the 2.5-3.5s it is down, then E2-hook into Q-W. Doran's Shield blunts his Overload spam. Force the all-in before his Tear finishes stacking.

edits.before: Steal Realm Warp at 6 and hold it — it strips his escape and gives you a global while he has nothing
edits.after: Bait Spell Flux off him first — without Flux his Rune Prison only slows, and the all-in survives it

edits.before: - Ryze Rune Prison (Root): matchup-defining — Point-blank root — respect the EQ chain that follows it. Count it out loud if you must. - Your E1 shield has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Ryze Rune Prison: matchup-defining — 615 range on a 9-11s cooldown, and it only roots if Spell Flux is on you. Bait the Flux and it is a slow. - Your E1 shield has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - Spell Flux is back every 2.5-3.5s, so it is not the gate.

edits.before: Point-blank root — respect the EQ chain that follows it. Until it’s spent, every commit is a coin flip.
edits.after: Rune Prison is 615 range and roots only through Spell Flux — with no Flux on you it is a slow you can eat.

edits.before: Track Ryze’s Rune Prison (Root): Point-blank root — respect the EQ chain that follows it. Forward steps wait for its downtime.
edits.after: Track Ryze’s Spell Flux: it is what upgrades Rune Prison from a slow to a root at 615 range. No Flux on you, no root — step in clean.

edits.before: Engaging with both E charges spent — no shield, no stun, and you're a melee mage standing in the open.
edits.after: Engaging with both E charges spent — no shield, no gap-close, and you are a melee mage inside Overload range.

edits.before: Both E charges spent means no shield and no exit — you're a melee mage in the open.
edits.after: Overload is 1000 range on a 5s cooldown that his other spells reset — you lose it.

edits.before: Engaging with both E charges spent — no shield, no stun, and you're a melee mage standing in the open.
edits.after: Realm Warp is a 180s portal, not a burst ult — hold it for a dive or a reposition, never for a solo duel.

notes: The worst error on this page was structural, not cosmetic: three separate fields claimed that hijacking Realm Warp leaves Ryze 'with no escape and no global'. Sylas's ultimate copies, it does not strip, so Ryze keeps his R and Sylas gains the single least useful ultimate in the game for a duel. That premise is what put level 6 in the Sylas column against the packet chart and against the already-audited mirror; fixed as a matched pair. Second real correction: Rune Prison is 615 range and only roots through Spell Flux — 'point-blank root' appears in three more fields I did not have room to edit (breakdown.wave, breakdown.feeding, report[9].t) and should be swept if there is a later pass.
